title: Presigned S3 URLs can be retargeted across virtual-host buckets through X-Forwarded-Host
summary:
### Summary
_Short summary of the problem. Make the impact and severity as clear as possible. For example: An unsafe deserialization vulnerability allows any unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary code on the server._

### Details
SeaweedFS verifies SigV4 presigned requests using client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host, while routing and IAM select the bucket from the actual Host. A URL for one bucket can therefore be retargeted to another bucket authorized to the signing identity.

### PoC
On SeaweedFS 4.46, enable -s3.domainName=s3.test. Create alpha-bkt and beta-bkt with different contents at shared.txt, using a signer authorized for both. Generate a virtual-host presigned GET for alpha-bkt/shared.txt. The original URL returns alpha’s data. Changing Host to beta-bkt.s3.test returns 403; adding X-Forwarded-Host: alpha-bkt.s3.test:<port> returns 200 with beta’s data. The same technique retargets a presigned PUT. A signer authorized only for alpha receives 403.

### Impact
A presigned-URL bearer can read or modify the same signed key in other buckets accessible to the signing identity without knowing its secret. Method, key, expiry, and IAM permissions remain enforced.
